ratings_why.fun: Every turn asks what to play last and where to seat it, and the fight pays off with a visible storm of Gusts and a Thunderhead finish; you'd happily draft it.
ratings_why.distinct: Announced (the last unit you played, any tribe) is new and makes play order the shop puzzle; out-of-turn attacks alone are more familiar.

verdict_why: The two keywords now read cleanly and the rulings cover the edge cases; what's left is wording polish, not a real fix.

points.text: Lady High Pressure's "after each one, your Announced unit Gusts instead" reads oddly after attacks that didn't happen; "each of the enemy's first 3 normal attacks is skipped, and your Announced unit Gusts instead" says the same thing plainly.
Old Föhn's "count for none of the enemy's cards" is hard to parse at a glance; "the enemy's own cards ignore these Gusts" carries it in fewer words.
Sir Vane is the best fantasy in the tribe but needs a ruling card to read; show the copied unit's text on his card face in the UI so players never have to remember it.

Gust Page's quarrel (only one of them gets to go first) is lovely flavour, but a second Page is a blank card; maybe the Pages that lose the quarrel gain something small, so the squabble shows on the board.
A late fight can fire 15 or more Gusts; a visible Gust queue and the Thunder counter matter more for reading this tribe than any card wording.

standouts.why: The Helm, who mentions his name to everyone, is always Announced: the lore is the rule, and it reads in one line.
The Thunderhead arrives late and loud, counting the storm, and the Crier setting him off early is a puzzle a player can see coming.
Mr and Mrs Fair-and-Foul are never home together, and the two-state card says that with gold one turn and a Gust the next.

weakest.why: The Bag-Bearer is just a delivery for the Bag of Winds; no court character comes through in what it does.
The Barometer Clerk asks the player to remember last fight's Gust count, with a fallback mode on top; the most bookkeeping for the least story.
Extra Gust Pages and any earlier Start of Combat Gust turn it into a vanilla 2/3, which may feel like a misread to a new Gale player.

flags.note: Sir Vane copying a Tier 6 capstone (or golden Vane copying two) is the tribe's biggest swing; the designer already names the fallback.
The Warden with the Helm puts up to +20/+20 a fight on each of two Announced units, more if Sir Vane copies the Warden.
